newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary feed wheat up, other grains mostly flat.
newsitem.headline: Hungary feed wheat up, other grains mostly flat.

text.p: Feed wheat futures prices on the Budapest Commodity Exchange (BCE) rose for most maturities on Friday due to a temporary lack of supply, traders said.
"Earlier sales of lower quality left over from milling wheat (spot) purchases ran out," said Gabor Herczeg of LaSalle.
Feed wheat prices rose rose by between 50 and 400 forints for all maturities, with all three 1998 maturities, January, March and May, rising the daily allowed 400 forints per tonne.
September feed wheat finished at 17,200 forints, December at 18,800 and May at 20,560.
Milling wheat futures were steady to higher as the market was divided on the quality of this year's crop, Herczeg said.
"One report suggested that out of 400,000 tonnes sampled, only 40,000 tonnes would meet euro standards, and 10,000 tonnes milling standards," Herczeg said.
However, another market view did not fully agree with excessive quality fears.
"The other view is that the mills might go for wheat that falls just short of BCE milling wheat standards but would still be useable and some 3,000 forints (per tonne) cheaper," Herczeg said.
"I think that in the long run the latter opinion could prove right," he said.
Milling wheat futures finished 80 to 270 forints higher for maturities until May 1998, except for December which remained steady.
Maize futures were steady to slightly higher, with the exception of the May 1998 maturity which went limit-up to 20,930 forints but in an insignificant turnover of five contracts.
Total turnover was a below-average 722 lots or 381.9 million forints, up from Thursday's 444 lots or 238 million forints.
Milling wheat accounted for the lion's share of the turnover with 491 lots.
